topic.title: Elite C++ Mechanics II
topic.description: More deep dives into obscure C++ rules, memory management, and advanced features.

questions.title: Type Punning with Unions
questions.explanation: Reading from a different union member than the one last written to is technically undefined behavior in C++ (unlike C). However, the bit pattern of 3.14f interpreted as an int will definitely not be zero, so it prints NZ.

questions.title: Static Local Variable Initialization Thread Safety
questions.explanation: In C++11 and later, static local variable initialization is thread-safe and guaranteed to happen exactly once. 'init()' is only called the first time func() is executed.

questions.title: Default Arguments on Virtual Functions (Revisited)
questions.explanation: b.f() uses B's default argument (1) but calls D's function dynamically (D1). d.f() uses D's default argument (2) and calls D's function (D2).

questions.title: Pointer to Array vs Array of Pointers
questions.explanation: Assuming a 64-bit system: p is a single pointer (8 bytes). q is an array of 5 pointers (5 * 8 = 40 bytes).

questions.title: Virtual Base Class Constructor Call
questions.explanation: The constructor of a virtual base class (V) is called by the most derived class (C). A's and B's calls to V's constructor are ignored.

questions.title: Function Try Blocks
questions.explanation: A function try block catches exceptions from member initializers. It prints 'C'. However, function try blocks on constructors ALWAYS rethrow the exception automatically, which is then caught in main printing 'M'.

questions.title: Overload Resolution: Exact Match vs Conversion
questions.explanation: Float to double is a promotion (preferred), while float to int is a conversion (less preferred). Thus, f(double) is called.

questions.title: ADL (Argument-Dependent Lookup)
questions.explanation: Because of ADL, the compiler finds NS::func. It also finds the global func. Both are exact matches for the arguments, leading to an ambiguous call error at compile time.

questions.title: std::vector<bool> Specialization
questions.explanation: std::vector<bool> is a bit-packed specialization. v[0] does not return a bool&, but a proxy object (std::vector<bool>::reference). Since 'auto' deduces the proxy type, changing v[0] changes the underlying bit, which 'ref' still points to.

questions.title: String Literal Concatenation
questions.explanation: Adjacent string literals separated only by whitespace are concatenated at compile time.

questions.title: Exception in Destructor
questions.explanation: In C++11, destructors are noexcept by default. Throwing from a destructor that doesn't explicitly specify noexcept(false) immediately calls std::terminate, killing the program before 'C' can be printed. (Note: output may just be a crash, but prediction is conceptually Terminate).

questions.title: Typeid on Polymorphic Types
questions.explanation: Because B has a virtual function (the destructor), it is a polymorphic type. typeid(*p) evaluates at runtime to the dynamic type, which is D. Therefore, they are equal (1).

questions.title: Typeid on Non-Polymorphic Types
questions.explanation: Because B has no virtual functions, it is non-polymorphic. typeid(*p) evaluates at compile time to the static type, which is B. They are not equal (0).

questions.title: Anonymous Namespaces
questions.explanation: Variables in an anonymous namespace are effectively global to the translation unit, accessible via the global scope resolution operator ::x.

questions.title: Final keyword
questions.explanation: The 'final' keyword prevents further overriding in derived classes, but it is a valid override of A's function, so dynamic dispatch calls B's function.

questions.title: Decltype with Parentheses
questions.explanation: decltype(a) yields int. However, decltype((a)) yields an lvalue reference to int (int&). Thus, modifying b modifies a.

questions.title: Template Non-Type Parameters
questions.explanation: Template non-type parameters must be known at compile time. Since 5 is a literal, print<5>() is perfectly valid.

questions.title: Mutable Keyword
questions.explanation: The 'mutable' keyword allows a member variable to be modified even if the object is const or the member function is const.

questions.title: Delete Operator Overloading
questions.explanation: When 'delete n' is called, it calls the destructor (which is trivial and prints nothing) and then calls the overloaded class-specific operator delete, printing K.

questions.title: Explicit Constructor
questions.explanation: The explicit constructor prevents implicit conversions (like pass(10)). Directly calling the constructor Num n1(5) is allowed, printing N.

questions.title: Lambda return type deduction
questions.explanation: C++14 allows lambdas to deduce their return type if all return statements return the same type. Both 1 and 2 are ints, so it works perfectly.

questions.title: Virtual functions inside Constructors
questions.explanation: During the Base constructor, the object is technically only a Base (the Derived parts haven't been built yet). Therefore, dynamic dispatch does not reach down to Derived, and Base::foo is called.

questions.title: Address of Operator Overloading
questions.explanation: The unary address-of operator (&) can be overloaded. Taking the address of t invokes the overloaded operator, printing &.

questions.title: Global vs Member operator new
questions.explanation: By prefixing 'new' with '::', it forces the global allocator to be used, completely bypassing the class-specific overloaded operator new. Thus, nothing is printed.

questions.title: Rvalue Reference to Lvalue Reference
questions.explanation: std::move casts the lvalue reference 'b' to an rvalue reference 'c'. 'c' still refers to the same memory location as 'a' and 'b'. Modifying 'c' modifies 'a'.
